headline: Spatial niches and cell states resolved from spatial transcriptomic and chromatin data
label: Spatial Niche Transcriptomic Attribution
summary: Spatial tools now test niche-dependent expression, domain boundaries, and cell-state versus cell-type identity in situ.
synthesis: The dominant thread is attributing transcriptomic variation to spatial context rather than to cell identity alone. Kontext jointly represents cells and their local environments to identify spatial domains via ligand-receptor interactions, and smoothclust pairs spatial-smoothing domain clustering with a boundary density metric summarizing label transitions on spatial graphs. TRACER targets rare and fine-grained spatial domains, while SpaceDX localizes spatial patterns within subject-level differential expression testing. ARCADE separates cell-type abundance from continuous intratype state, and SpatioCAD uses a cell-density-aware graph diffusion model to pinpoint spatially variable genes. FICTURE2 infers the transcriptional program of individual RNA molecules from gene identity and spatial context. A zonated hepatocyte study reports an invariant cell-type sub-network with broadly expressed regulators distinguishing cell-type from cell-state identity. What is new is boundary-level summarization and spatially conditioned testing of expression. Chromatin-focused items, including HiCONA and C-Fetch, address 3D genome organization and sit outside this thread.
